html:
The Siege of Belgrade was an Ottoman attack on the Hungarian held fortress of Belgrade in July 1456, three years after Mehmed II took Constantinople. The defence was led by John Hunyadi, regent of Hungary.

Hunyadi broke the Ottoman river blockade with a fleet, and the friar John of Capistrano brought thousands of crusaders, mostly peasants. When the Ottoman assault reached the town, the defenders threw it back, then counterattacked and took the sultan's camp. Mehmed was wounded and withdrew. Belgrade held until 1521. Hunyadi died of plague weeks later. Pope Callixtus III had ordered church bells rung at noon to call for prayer for the defenders; the noon bell came to be remembered as a celebration of the victory.
sum: The Siege of Belgrade was an Ottoman attack on the Hungarian held fortress of Belgrade in July 1456, three years after Mehmed II took Constantinople. The defence was led by John Hunyadi, regent of Hungary.
